noveltyJustification: 13 of 18 findings are new external evidence from the edition model, the upgrade docs, the routines and approvals docs, and the licence files; 5 are new synthesis that fixes the skip list and the build order.

label: OpenBot has exactly two editions: OPENBOT_EDITION=personal runs it for one person on their own machine with nobody signed in and one computer, while unset or team is OpenBot as an organization runs it.
Even the personal edition runs PostgreSQL, the one computer and the server, and no supervisor and no bundled Bot containers.
The Kubernetes part is release promotion: a kubernetes plan|apply|gitops command around an openbot Helm chart that checks the manifest image digest and chart archive checksum before invoking Helm.
The managed-upgrade part is a management agent the openbot chart installs into the cluster, connecting to CopilotKit's management service by default.
The mobile part is a full React Native app of 632 files under mobile/.
A routine is a standing instruction a Bot carries out on a schedule instead of waiting to be asked, and its reply lands in a channel like any other message.
Routines, goals and check-ins are one list drawn from three stores, and every row is the same sentence in four parts: What it is, Starts, Does and Until.

Approvals resolve in a fixed order where the first answer wins (kinds of action, rules, auto-review, extra vigilant), and the strictest matching rule wins so a team rule that asks beats anything the person allowed.
Six kinds of action ask in every edition whatever the person's own switch says: deleting, sending to other people, sharing, posting, paying, and changing a password or account settings.
Licences: OpenBot, OpenGhost and hermes-muse are MIT; OpenMausBot, rakazo, turnstone and buzz are Apache-2.0; openhuman is GPL-3.0.
openhuman's GPL-3.0 means its TUI code cannot be lifted into a permissively licensed tree: only its shape (four tabs, overlay approvals, six activity statuses) is reusable.

The skip list with a reason each: Kubernetes (release promotion for a cluster a small team does not run), managed upgrades (a vendor agent tied to that chart), multi-tenant (memory scoped per organization when a small team is one organization), enterprise roles (an admin tier governing a sign-in that does not exist), mobile (632 files for a client that cannot run a launchd job), and PostgreSQL plus Compose (a database server and container supervisor where the runtime is a Node CLI with a SQLite index).

The reuse inventory with repo, path and licence: OpenBot's four-part routine sentence (docs/routines.md:16, MIT), OpenBot's approvals precedence ladder (docs/approvals.md:3, MIT), OpenBot's derived review state and idempotent approve (api/openapi/learning.yaml:1130, MIT), OpenGhost's bounded memory with a tidy rewrite (memory.js:11, MIT), and hermes-muse's staged-write pinning rule (skills/companion/references/memory.md:20, MIT).
Four of the five reusable items are documents or patterns rather than code: the parts worth copying are the rules, and the code that enforces them is small enough to write.

The ranked build order, smallest first: the memory store, the memory review item, the skill proposal store, the memory source sync, routines as sentences, the approvals ladder, and the terminal client last.

The memory store comes first because it is the only item that adds a new file shape and every later item reads it: the review item reviews a fact, the proposal store reviews a skill, and the sync writes facts.
The terminal client comes last because it draws the four surfaces the earlier items create, and building it first would mean drawing empty screens.
The whole build is seven items, none of which needs a new service, a database server, a container or a sign-in.

reason: GPL-3.0 cannot be relicensed into this tree, so only the shape transfers.
Its native side installs and supervises Compose, which this runtime does not have.
A small team is one organization, so the second scope would be a branch nothing takes.
It would draw four empty surfaces until the memory, review, proposal and routine items exist.
